name: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
instruments: MEDA, Mastcam-Z, SuperCam, PIXL, SHERLOC, MOXIE, RIMFAX, Ingenuity Helicopter
scientific_summary: Landed near the western fan-delta of Jezero Crater (18.4457°N, 77.4508°E) to investigate ancient lacustrine biosignatures, cache rock core samples at Three Forks Sample Depot, demonstrate MOXIE oxygen production, and record MEDA surface weather.

name: MSL Curiosity Rover (Bradbury Landing)
instruments: RAD, ChemCam, Mastcam, SAM, CheMin, MAHLI, APXS, REMS, DAN
scientific_summary: Landed in Quad 51 (Yellowknife) of Aeolis Palus inside Gale Crater (-4.5895°N, 137.4417°E). Confirmed ancient freshwater habitable lake environments, organic molecules, and measured surface ionizing radiation via RAD (0.64 ± 0.12 mSv/day).

name: InSight Geophysical Lander
mission_name: InSight (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport)
instruments: SEIS (Seismometer), HP3 (Heat Flow Probe), RISE, TWINS
scientific_summary: Detected over 1,300 marsquakes and constrained Mars's internal structure: ~50 km average crust (32 km north / 58 km south), ~1,860 km mantle, and ~1,480 km radius liquid iron-nickel-sulfur core.

name: Viking 1 Lander (Thomas Mutch Memorial Station)
instruments: GCMS, Biology Package (LR, PR, GEX), Meteorology Boom, XRFS
scientific_summary: First spacecraft to successfully operate long-term on the Martian surface (2,245 sols), transmitting the first surface color panoramas, long-term meteorological records (150–250 K), and soil composition analyses.

name: Viking 2 Lander (Gerald Soffen Memorial Station)
scientific_summary: Operated for 1,281 sols on the boulder-strewn northern plains of Utopia Planitia (48.269°N, 134.010°E), documenting seasonal winter water-ice surface frost.

name: Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner Rover (Carl Sagan Memorial Station)
scientific_summary: Delivered Sojourner, humanity's first wheeled rover on Mars, onto an ancient flood plain at the mouth of Ares Vallis (19.33°N, 326.45°E), returning 16,500 lander images and 15 rock/soil chemical analyses.

name: MER-A Spirit Rover (Columbia Memorial Station)
instruments: Pancam, Mini-TES, Mossbauer, APXS, Microscopic Imager, RAT
scientific_summary: Explored Gusev Crater and the Columbia Hills (-14.5718°N, 175.4785°E) for 2,210 sols, discovering opaline silica and carbonate rocks formed by ancient hydrothermal aqueous activity.

name: MER-B Opportunity Rover (Challenger Memorial Station)
instruments: Pancam, Mini-TES, Mossbauer, APXS, Microscopic Imager, RAT
scientific_summary: Operated for 5,111 sols and traversed >45 km from Eagle and Victoria Craters to Endeavour Crater (-1.9462°N, 354.4734°E), discovering hematite 'blueberries' and sulfate evaporites deposited in ancient acidic water.

name: Phoenix Mars Lander (Green Valley)
instruments: Robotic Arm, TEGA, MECA, SSI, MET
scientific_summary: Excavated shallow arctic trenches at 68.22°N, 234.30°E (validated by THEMIS and HiRISE), directly exposing shallow subsurface water ice and detecting perchlorate salts and calcium carbonate.

name: Tianwen-1 Lander & Zhurong Rover
instruments: RoPeR Subsurface Radar, MarSCoDe, MSCam, NaTeCam, MCS
scientific_summary: Landed in southern Utopia Planitia (25.1°N, 109.9°E), using ground-penetrating radar to map layered subsurface regolith and polygonal terrain features.

name: Ingenuity Helicopter (Wright Brothers Field)
instruments: RTE Color Aerial Camera, Navcam, Laser Altimeter
scientific_summary: First powered, controlled aircraft flight on another planet (April 19, 2021 at Wright Brothers Field, ICAO code JZRO), performing aerial reconnaissance of raised ridges and boulder fields ahead of Perseverance.

name: Three Forks Sample Return Depot
scientific_summary: First off-world sample depot established on flat terrain near the base of the Jezero western fan-delta, holding 10 sealed igneous, sedimentary, and regolith tubes for future Mars Sample Return pickup.
